The Find My app is used by millions of people to locate lost devices in emergencies, and even more share their real-time location with friends and family through it.

The iOS 27 system update brings several changes that improve the Find My experience. Specifically, iPhone users who usually only wear their Apple Watch when going out for a walk will automatically benefit from smarter location sharing…

In iOS 26 and earlier, location sharing in Find My relies on only one device. Users can choose one device in Find My settings as their location source—that's all. For most people, that device is their iPhone.

So your location on the Find My map depends entirely on the actual location of your iPhone. But if you're a heavy user who tends to leave your phone at home and often uses your Apple Watch on its own, this setup isn't very practical.

In iOS 27, Apple has improved this. Now, if you use Find My on your iPhone and have a paired Apple Watch, when the watch is not near the phone, Find My will automatically use the watch's location. This means location sharing will proactively update to reflect where you actually are.

The automatic location sharing feature on Apple Watch applies to both the standard version and models with cellular capability, but there's no denying that the cellular version can more reliably send location information to the Find My network.

watchOS 27 also gives the Find My app on Apple Watch a major redesign. The previously separate Find Items, Find People, and Find Devices apps have been removed, replaced by a new unified Find My app. The new app features a refreshed user interface with a full-screen map layout, allowing users to switch between items easily by turning the Digital Crown.

iOS 27 and watchOS 27 are currently in beta and will be released as a free update to all users this autumn (expected in September).
